meta.note:
Copy to private.json (gitignored), replace these with queries naming real identifiers, and run:

    python -m tests.relevance.eval --vault /media/Share/Vault --queries tests/relevance/private.json --baseline tests/relevance/private.baseline.private.json --embedder ollama

This is where the README's measured claims belong - 'dense retrieval scores 0/40 on exact identifiers where BM25 scores 40/40' is a sentence today and should be a run. Forty identifier queries against the real corpus is what makes it one.

Keep one baseline per corpus: a rank measured against the fixture with the hashing embedder is not comparable to one measured here, and eval.py refuses to compare across either.

queries.q: <a registration, policy number or account number from the real vault>
queries.why: The claim worth re-running: exact identifiers are the lexical arm's job and the dense arm cannot do them.

queries.q: <a question phrased the way you would actually ask it>
queries.why: Only meaningful with --embedder ollama; the hashing embedder has no semantics.
